findings.title: Stable Channel Update for Desktop
findings.summary_md: The vendor advisory behind the story headline, posted September 22, 2026, promoted Chrome 154 to stable as 154.0.8037.57/.58 for Windows and Mac and 154.0.8037.57 for Linux with 108 security fixes, 11 of them critical. The criticals are all memory-safety defects: three ANGLE buffer overflows including CVE-2026-95350 (a $5,000 bounty, reported by STAR Labs researchers on 2026-08-24), CVE-2026-95281, and CVE-2026-95284, plus GPU out-of-bounds writes, WebGL bugs, and use-after-free defects in ServiceWorker, Fullscreen, WindowDialog, and AdFilter. It also credits OpenAI Codex Security researcher amyb with two V8 bugs, CVE-2026-95304 and CVE-2026-95306, reported on 2026-09-12, and notes bug details may stay restricted until a majority of users are updated.

findings.title: Extended Stable Update for Desktop
findings.summary_md: Posted September 22, 2026 alongside the Chrome 154 promotion, this advisory updated the Extended Stable channel to 152.0.7977.140 for Windows and Mac. Enterprise fleets pinned two milestones back received their fixed build on the same day as the 108-fix promotion rather than with the September 29 point release.
